name: Reducing alcohol and salt for eye redness
lead: Cutting back on alcohol and salty foods is a lifestyle habit people use to get whiter, less bloodshot-looking eyes and a less puffy face. Clear sclera are part of looking rested and healthy, and people in appearance communities track which habits show up in their eyes.

Red eye has many causes, including conjunctivitis, dry eye, irritants, tiredness, and medications or recreational drugs [1]. Practitioners report that nights with drinking or heavy salt are followed by redder eyes and facial puffiness, and they adjust intake accordingly. Alcohol and dietary sodium are not listed among the causes in the general reference used here, so the connection rests on personal reports.

chain: Drink less alcohol and eat less salt
Fewer triggers for redness and puffiness
angle.text: People who notice redder eyes after drinking or salty meals cut back to see whiter eyes. Sleep and hydration are commonly paired with the change.

paras: The habit means limiting alcohol, especially in the evening, and moderating salty or processed food, sometimes alongside more sleep and water. Users compare how their eyes look in the mornings after changes.

Reference sources list conjunctivitis, dry eye, blepharitis, airborne irritants, tiredness and some drugs as causes, and note that eye pain, vision loss, light sensitivity or injury need urgent medical care [1].

card.summary: Drinking less alcohol and eating less salt to get whiter, less bloodshot, less puffy eyes.
card.note: Persistent or painful red eye warrants medical assessment.

quick.overview:
This habit means cutting back on alcohol and salty food to see less red, bloodshot eyes and less puffiness.

People tend to notice the difference the morning after and adjust.
quick.mechanism: Practitioners say alcohol and salt are followed by redder eyes and puffiness. Red eye has many causes, including dry eye and irritation.
quick.risks: Low risk. Persistent redness, pain or vision changes call for a clinician.
